title: DR1 offers only the trader's own GB branch addresses as the consignment contact; the frontend offers the whole address book, overseas consignors included.

finding.frontend: The contact page offers `addressBook.all(orgId)` — every record in the organisation's book, in book order (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/contact/controller.js:69-74). fe-contact shows thirteen radios, the same thirteen records the party pickers page through, and they include Astra Rosales in Switzerland, Danish Meat Export ApS in Denmark, Laiterie du Nord SARL in France and Iberian Swine SA in Spain. So a trader can name a Spanish exporter as the person responsible for the consignment once it is inside Great Britain, and nothing on the page discourages it. The address book holds no type by which the list could be narrowed — the service says so in its own contract, "Addresses have no type in the address book (D3) — the same record may be a consignor on one notification and a consignee on the next" (src/server/app/services/address-book/index.js:12-15).
finding.prototype: DR1 draws this list from a separate collection of branch addresses, not from the consignment address book the pickers use (app/data/contact-addresses.js:1-21, rendered at app/views/contact-address-for-consignment.html:68-83). dr1-contact-address-for-consignment shows three, all in Great Britain: Aberdeen Livestock Ltd in Aberdeen, West Country Livestock Ltd in Bristol, Cymru Animal Imports Ltd in Cardiff. The page says what the list is for — the person responsible for the consignment from when it enters Great Britain — and the help line names the collection when it tells the trader where a missing one comes from: "add a new branch address" (:65).
finding.difference: Narrow the contact list to the trader's own branch addresses. That needs the address book to distinguish a branch record from a party record, which today it deliberately does not, so the API and the record shape have to change before the page can. Until then the page offers a choice DR1 rules out, and the frontend's own hint does not warn against it. The narrower question of what the page says the contact is for is a separate copy change on the same page.
finding.falsifiedBy: A DR1 contact list drawn from the same address collection as the consignment pickers, or an address-book record carrying a type or category the frontend could filter on today.
finding.correction: Verified, no change; both lists were counted rather than inferred. The frontend page renders thirteen radios, and the four overseas records the finding names are all there — Astra Rosales in Bern, Danish Meat Export ApS in Copenhagen, Laiterie du Nord SARL in Lille and Iberian Swine SA in Huesca. DR1 renders three, all United Kingdom, and its source collection holds exactly those three and nothing else, headed "Branch addresses available for contact address selection". The two collections are genuinely separate: DR1's consignment pickers draw from a thirty-three-record collection whose records each carry a `type`, and the contact page does not touch it. The needs-backend band is argued rather than assumed and the argument holds — the frontend's own stub book carries no type, category or use on any record, so there is nothing to filter on without a record-shape change, which is the same gap the picker role-scoping finding runs into.

relatedTo.why: the sentence DR1 opens the page with is what tells the trader why the list is narrow
DR1's contact help line is the add path for this collection specifically
